'''Decipher tournament T-shirts''' were T-shirts that [[Decipher]] made as tournament prizes and for volunteers during the years it published ''Star Wars'' CCG. [[Jim Colson]], who started running tournaments in 1996, when Decipher was shipping T-shirts as part of the prize support, wrote that he handed out over 200 of them. In February 2003 he posted a list of the shirts on the Players Committee forum, and he updated it until October 2003.<ref name="pcf-5796-113117">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=113117#113117 Trade/Collecting Questions], Jim Colson (ShadowLeader), posts of February 2003 (last edited 28 October 2003) reposted by Scott Lingrell (CRingwell), Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (13 December 2005). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20060618084301/http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?t=5796&postdays=0&postorder=asc&start=100 Internet Archive]</ref>

== Card-art tournament T-shirts ==

According to Colson, the tournament shirts had a large picture of a card on the front, usually a logo such as "use the force" on the back and a ''Star Wars'' logo on one sleeve. The early shirts were white cotton and the later ones "athletic gray" cotton. Most of the white shirts were printed in bulk; he estimated about 1000 of each, unless a shirt was made for a smaller, specific event.<ref name="pcf-5796-113117" /> He listed them in the basic order of release:

Decipher also made World Championship finalist shirts with a large ''Star Wars'' CCG logo: a white shirt for the [[1998 Decipher World Championship|1998 World Championship]] and a black one for the [[1999 Decipher World Championship|1999 World Championship]], each given to the top 12 players, with "only 20?" made of each.<ref name="pcf-5796-113117" />

== Other Decipher Star Wars games ==

Colson also listed the shirts of Decipher's other ''Star Wars'' card games. For [[Young Jedi]], Decipher made two black promotional shirts, given out as prizes at conventions and to demo volunteers: the first had a red theme after the Menace of Darth Maul set and the second a blue theme after the Jedi Council set. Two gray shirts with the card images of Qui-Gon Jinn (Menace of Darth Maul) and Darth Maul (Enhanced Menace of Darth Maul) went to DecipherCon 2000 and 2002 tournament winners, 100 of each. For the [[Jedi Knights Trading Card Game]], a black "Strike Team" shirt was given to hundreds of volunteers who helped promote the game's launch.<ref name="pcf-5796-113117" />

== Shirts without the Star Wars logo ==

In May 2003 Colson listed the Decipher shirts that were related to ''Star Wars'' but carried no ''Star Wars'' logo:<ref name="pcf-5796-113119">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=113119#113119 Trade/Collecting Questions], Jim Colson (ShadowLeader), post of 16 May 2003 reposted by Scott Lingrell (CRingwell), Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (13 December 2005). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20060618084301/http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?t=5796&postdays=0&postorder=asc&start=100 Internet Archive]</ref>
* 1998: black Decipher Customizable Card Group shirt, given to volunteers doing ''Star Wars'' CCG, Young Jedi, Jedi Knights and ''Star Trek'' demos at conventions.
* 1999: black Decipher Demo Crew 1999 shirt, given to the same volunteers; black long-sleeved Shawn Valdez '99 shirt, given to tournament directors, buyers and donors during the Shawn Valdez fundraiser campaign; black [[DecipherCon 1999|DecipherCon '99]] attendee shirt; black DecipherCon '99 staff shirt, given to all staff including volunteers; white Decipher Tournament Director shirt, sent to every new ''Star Wars'' CCG tournament director of 1999 and 2000.
* 2000: tan [[DecipherCon 2000|DecipherCon 2K]] staff shirt, given to all staff including volunteers; DecipherCon 2K attendee shirt.

He wrote that there was some debate, between himself and Steve Sansweet, over whether the long-sleeved Shawn Valdez '99 shirt was a ''Star Wars'' collectible, because it had no ''Star Wars'' logo and did not really fall under Decipher's licensing agreement with Lucasfilm; he called it "Definately a Decipher Collectible".<ref name="pcf-5796-113119" />

== 2005 collectors' list ==

In June 2005 [[Brandon Ruck]] posted a list of the tournament shirts he was looking for, with edits by Colson. It calls the gray Lord Vader shirt from DecipherCon 2000 "very rare" and states that a Chewbacca shirt does not exist.<ref name="pcf-5796-83333">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=83333#83333 Trade/Collecting Questions], Brandon Ruck (newhorizans), with edits by Jim Colson, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (15 June 2005). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20060618084051/http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=81971 Internet Archive]</ref>
